source_text: Gratia Dei per Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum. Igitur ego ipse mente servio legi Dei, carne autem legi peccati. Gloria Christo. Amen.
orientation: Paul, having cried out for deliverance from the body of death, now gives thanks to God through Jesus Christ and states his divided service.
pass_a_gloss: Grace of God through Jesus Christ our Lord. Therefore I myself with the mind serve the law of God, but with the flesh the law of sin. Glory to Christ. Amen.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'grace' for gratia, and the genitive Dei is rendered as 'of God' to preserve the source's noun phrase structure.
The preposition per is rendered as 'through' to show the means by which grace comes, and the full title is kept in source order.
Igitur is rendered as 'therefore' to mark the conclusion from the preceding cry, and ipse as 'myself' to emphasize Paul's personal statement.

choices.english: with the mind serve the law of God
choices.why: The ablative mente is rendered as 'with the mind' to show the instrument or sphere of service, and servio as 'serve' to keep the verb's active force.
rejected: in my mind serve God's law
serve the law of God with my mind

choices.english: but with the flesh the law of sin
choices.why: The contrast autem is rendered as 'but', and the ablative carne as 'with the flesh' to parallel 'with the mind', keeping the two spheres distinct.
rejected: but in the flesh the law of sin
but the flesh serves the law of sin

choices.why: The dative Christo is rendered as 'to Christ' to show the recipient of the doxology, preserving the brief exclamation's force.

bible_refs.note: Gratia Dei per Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum. Igitur ego ipse mente servio legi Dei, carne autem legi peccati.

pass_b_english: Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself serve the law of God with my mind, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin. Glory to Christ. Amen.
